Generate data from a fitted model

Source: R/ctGenerateFromFit.R
ctGenerateFromFit.Rd

Adds a $generated object to a fit, holding random data generated from the fit's posterior (or its estimate), on either backend. ctStanGenerateFromFit is maintained as a backward-compatible alias.

Usage

ctGenerateFromFit(
  fit,
  nsamples = 200,
  fullposterior = FALSE,
  verboseErrors = FALSE,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L),
  intoverstates = "fit",
  effects = c("population", "fitted")
)

Arguments

fit

A fit from ctFit, on either backend.

nsamples

Positive integer specifying number of datasets to generate.

fullposterior

Logical indicating whether to sample from the full posterior (original nsamples) or the posterior mean.

verboseErrors

if TRUE, print verbose output when errors in generation encountered.

cores

Number of cpu cores to use: R worker processes for a stan fit, and for a julia fit the engine threads its draws are generated on.

intoverstates

For backend='julia' fits, how the latent states are generated. 'fit' (the default) follows the fit. A fit with explicit states (intoverstates=FALSE) then generates states explicitly, and every other fit generates each observation from the Kalman filter's one-step-ahead prediction, the density the fit used. A generated dataset's llrow is then the likelihood under which it was generated.

FALSE simulates the model directly, whatever the fit used: each subject's trajectory from the process at its own parameters, and then each observation from its measurement model given the state, as ctGenerate does. The two differ for non-Gaussian indicators and for state dependent dynamics, where the filter is an approximation. Comparing data generated each way, with the same effects, shows the effect of that approximation, separately from any misfit of the model to the observed data. TRUE always generates through the filter.

In all cases the states are generated anew.

effects

For backend='julia' fits with random effects. 'population' (the default) draws new subjects, and groups at every level, from the fitted population distribution at each parameter draw, so the generated data are the model's prediction for a new sample with the same design. 'fitted' keeps the fitted subjects, each at its sampled effects when the fit sampled and saved them, and otherwise at its conditional mode. A fit with intoverpop='augmented' has no per-subject effects, so only 'population' applies. Stan fits generate as the fit was made, and give an error if the argument is set.

Value

The fit, with a $generated element: Y, the generated data as an array of sample by data row by manifest variable, on the original time and missingness structure, and llrow, each generated row's log likelihood.

Examples

gen <- ctGenerateFromFit(ctstantestfit, nsamples=3,fullposterior=TRUE,cores=1)
plot(gen$generated$Y[3,,2],type='l') #Third random data sample, 2nd manifest var, all time points.
